questions.text: What does perplexity measure in the context of evaluating a pretrained text generator?
options: The number of parameters in the model
The speed of text generation in tokens per second
How surprised the model is by held-out text — lower means better prediction
The diversity of generated text samples
questions.explanation: Perplexity = exp(cross-entropy loss). It represents the effective number of equally likely next tokens the model considers at each position. Lower perplexity means the model assigns higher probability to the actual next token, indicating better language modeling.

questions.text: Why is it insufficient to evaluate a text generator using only perplexity?
options: Perplexity is too expensive to compute
Perplexity measures prediction accuracy but not output quality aspects like coherence, diversity, or factual correctness
Perplexity only works for classification models
Perplexity requires human evaluators to compute
questions.explanation: Perplexity captures how well the model predicts the training distribution but says nothing about whether generated text is coherent, diverse, factual, or useful. A model can have low perplexity while still producing repetitive or nonsensical outputs.

questions.text: What does the distinct-n metric measure in generated text?
options: The ratio of unique n-grams to total n-grams, indicating lexical diversity
The grammatical correctness of generated sentences
The semantic similarity to a reference text
The number of distinct topics covered in the output
questions.explanation: Distinct-n computes the proportion of unique n-grams (unigrams, bigrams, etc.) among all n-grams in the generated text. A low distinct-n score reveals repetitive generation, even if perplexity is acceptable.

questions.text: Which of the following are valid approaches to evaluating the quality of a pretrained text generator’s output?Select all that apply
options: Only checking if the model’s loss is below 1.0
Human evaluation of generated samples for coherence and fluency
Measuring diversity metrics (distinct-n, self-BLEU) alongside perplexity
Counting the total number of tokens generated
questions.explanation: Comprehensive evaluation combines automatic metrics (perplexity for prediction quality, distinct-n and self-BLEU for diversity) with human evaluation for coherence, fluency, and factual accuracy. Loss thresholds and token counts alone are not meaningful quality measures.

questions.text: What does a self-BLEU score measure when evaluating generated text diversity?
options: How similar the generated text is to a human reference
The perplexity of the model on its own outputs
The accuracy of the tokenizer on generated text
How similar different generated samples are to each other — lower means more diverse
questions.explanation: Self-BLEU computes BLEU scores between pairs of generated samples. High self-BLEU means the model produces very similar outputs across different prompts or seeds, indicating low diversity. Lower self-BLEU indicates the generator produces more varied text.
